q: A research report should typically place the recommendation:
o: At the end of the report
In the middle of the report
e: Lead with the call. The recommendation, target price, and 3-5 thesis bullets should be on the first page so a reader sees the conclusion in 30 seconds.

q: How long must research reports and supporting workings be retained by a registered RA?
e: 5 years is the mandated retention period under SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014. Includes reports, supporting research, communications, and personal trading records.

q: When distributing a research report to clients, the RA must:
o: Send to top clients first, smaller clients later
Send simultaneously to all entitled clients
e: Distribution must be simultaneous to all entitled clients — preferential timing creates an unfair advantage and would breach SEBI's fair-distribution requirement.

q: Which of these is a mandatory disclosure in every research report under SEBI (RA) Regulations 2014?
e: Mandatory disclosures include SEBI registration number, personal/firm holdings of the subject security, conflicts of interest, compensation from subject company, etc. Personal contact details are not disclosed.

q: Cooling-off period for an RA's personal trading in a recommended security is approximately:
o: 1 day before and 1 day after publication
30 days before and 5 days after publication
e: Per SEBI norms, the analyst cannot trade in the recommended security for ~30 days before publication (to prevent front-running) and ~5 days after (to prevent benefiting from the recommendation's market impact).

q: An 'Initiation of Coverage' report is typically:
e: Initiation reports are comprehensive first takes on a stock — 30-50 pages covering business, industry, financials, valuation, risks, scenarios. Quarterly notes are 4-8 pages; daily notes 1-2.
